newsitem.title: USA: SF Fed's Parry warns inflation may be set to rise.
newsitem.headline: SF Fed's Parry warns inflation may be set to rise.

text.p: While inflation has performed well recently, there is cause for some concern that it could move higher in the future, the head of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco said in a speech here Wednesday.
The core Consumer Price Index, which excludes food and energy prices, came in at 2.6 percent in 1996.
However, San Francisco Fed President Robert Parry said it is possible underlying inflation could be a full percentage point lower given overstatements to the CPI.
Still, in prepared remarks to the local chapter of the National Association of Business Economists, he indicated this was not a reason to become complacent.
"Are there still some issues to worry about regarding inflation?" Parry asked. "Well, for me, the immediate issue is that inflation could be set to rise in the future," he said.

Reiterating many of the remarks he made in a speech Tuesday, the San Francisco Fed chief emphasized the importance of not only preventing a rise in inflation and but also of working toward the goal of price stability, which means reducing inflation beyond its current level.
As he did Tuesday, Parry outlined special factors such as increased job insecurity and slower growth in benefits costs that have helped contain wage growth and inflation.
Still, he said the effects of these factors on inflation are likely to be temporary.

As a consequence, he said, "If resource utilization remains as high as it is now, we risk a modest pickup in inflation, and there's certainly little reason to think that inflation might fall further in the future."
Concerning the overall state of the economy, Parry said data on the fourth quarter have suggested strength, signaling that the slowdown in the third quarter may have been "just a 'pause.'"
"This suggests that 1997 is starting off with considerable momentum, and that the economy is likely to achieve at least its trend rate of growth," Parry said.
